static_traits.name: Li Mei
static_traits.occupation: Law school graduate preparing for the Lawyer qualification exam (aspiring to become a Lawyer)
static_traits.family_status: Both parents are Lawyers, no siblings
static_traits.social_status: Has a stable support system composed of parents, but because of inferiority avoids socializing with law school friends and colleagues
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problem history before multiple bar exam failures; no other psychotherapy received yet
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, able to describe traumatic events and emotional experiences specifically; positive attitude toward counseling, highly cooperative; tending toward self-blame and label-based expression (such as 'I am too stupid')

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling incompetent after multiple bar exam failures, doubting the ability to become a successful Lawyer.
basic_info.core_demands: The persistent sense of incompetence and Self-doubt have significantly affected my physical/mental health and motivation to continue in the legal profession, which prompted me to seek counseling; I do not want to be controlled by this Fear anymore. I just want to enjoy this sport again like before.
growth_experiences: Family occupational background: both parents are senior Lawyers, no siblings; long felt the need to reach parents' success standards in career choice and achievement, forming significant pressure and comparison.

Strong incompetence and Self-doubt began after the first bar exam failure; subsequent failures further Reinforced this experience; whenever thinking about the Lawyer profession, especially when contrasting with parents' success, the feeling intensifies markedly, affecting Learning motivation and daily functioning.

About a year ago was hit by a ball while playing softball, experiencing intense pain and fright; since then associating softball with injury, seeing softball games on TV or hearing friends talk about softball evokes Anxiety, and completely avoiding participating in the sport.

core_beliefs: I am not smart enough / not competent enough(I am incompetent)
Only by reaching my parents' standard of success am I worthy

special_situations.event: Receiving notice of yet another bar exam failure
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If failing multiple times, it proves I am not smart enough, never able to become a Lawyer
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Changing Learning methods, enrolling in different prep courses, doubling Learning to make up for 'inadequacy'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am too stupid, I cannot pass

special_situations.event: Talking with parents about career or thinking of parents' success
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach my parents' achievements, I will disappoint them, showing I am useless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding discussing unease and failure with parents, burying the pressure inside
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I let them down / I am not as good as them

special_situations.event: When facing socializing with law school friends/colleagues or hearing them talk about work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my performance is not like my peers', it is failure and shame
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids socializing with classmates and colleagues to reduce being compared and evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them / I am a failure

special_situations.event: Sees a softball game on TV or is invited to play softball
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I participate in softball again, injury will definitely happen again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Completely avoids softball-related situations and activities
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will get hurt as soon as I play, not worth the risk

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized by parents and seen as capable, proving oneself competent for the Lawyer profession and accepted
core_conflict.fear: Fears the shame of failure and being belittled; in sports, fears being injured again and losing control
defense_goal: Lowering shame and the risk of being denied by keeping distance and avoiding comparison
Not expressing vulnerability to parents to maintain self-esteem and surface stability

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, possibly judged a failure at any time
object_relations.object_representation: Parents/peers are authorities with high standards, judgment, and comparison

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing bar exam failures and Career development with parents or others
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing the other as a judge, believing oneself will be seen as not good enough (transference: being judged)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoiding emotional expression with factual, brief answers, quickly shifting the topic, lowering eye contact.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited or reminded to join softball activities
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes others ignore risks; if one participates, one will definitely be injured
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Politely but firmly declining with rationalizing phrasings (such as 'risks/costs are disproportionate').

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When seeing peers' career progress and involuntarily comparing
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding setbacks as core personal flaws, believing everything is 'I am not good'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using self-blaming and absolutist language (such as 'it is all my not-good'), lowering self-affirmation and help-seeking willingness.

manifestations: Avoids socializing with law-school friends and colleagues
Difficulty discussing incompetence and Self-doubt with parents
outcomes: Shame and Increased self-doubt, Decreased motivation

manifestations: Uses parents' success standards as the benchmark for self-worth, limiting room for choice
Fear of failure makes choices in career and leisure activities more constricted (avoiding social situations of retaking exams, avoiding softball)
outcomes: Inner conflict and Increased anxiety, actions hindered

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizes parents' success standards into the 'must / should' for evaluating herself, equating whether she passes exams with self-worth
On career topics, evaluates oneself by a success/failure dichotomy

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently using self-blaming and label-based language (such as 'I am too stupid')
Overly worrying about others' evaluations in relationships and socializing, leading to Withdrawal

exception_events.target_problem: When encountering or thinking about softball-related cues, Li Mei typically experiences strong Anxiety and chooses to avoid the sport.
exception_events.unique_outcome: When focused on Work or other hobbies, the sense of Fear markedly weakens, not controlled by softball-related Anxiety as usual.
exception_events.reason: Clue: attention occupied by other tasks, situational focus shifted, reducing evocation of injury memories and threat appraisal, thus Fear lessens.

positive_force: Family support system stable (parents can provide resources and support)
Able to persist in trying different prep methods and courses, showing some perseverance
Rationally knows injury is not inevitable (experience of playing safely for many past years)
Anxiety can drop markedly when attention is shifted, showing potential self-regulation ability
negative_force: Deep core belief of 'I am not smart enough / not as good as parents' and self-labeling
Tendency toward external comparison and seeking external validation, overly concerned with comparisons to parents and peers
Avoidance strategies (Avoids socializing and avoiding softball) create negative Reinforcement, maintaining the problem
Cognitive biases of catastrophizing and predicting the future (such as 'I will definitely get hurt again' 'I cannot pass the exam')
Self-criticism and Self-denial leading to declining motivation and Daily functioning

target_behavior.behavior: Fear of and avoidance of softball
antecedent: Seeing or thinking of a softball game (e.g. on television)
Friends talking about or inviting one to play softball
Recalling the pain and fright of being hit by a ball
target_behavior.core_reason: Associative learning after traumatic pain and fright, forming the catastrophic and predictive belief 're-engaging = will definitely be injured'
target_behavior.function: Avoiding perceived danger and the resulting Anxiety, briefly lowering discomfort
target_behavior.consequence: Unable to participate in the once-loved sport, increased Depression and loss, Fear maintained and Reinforced

antecedent: Talking about the bar exam or the legal profession
target_behavior.core_reason: Shame and Self-doubt after failure, fearing negative evaluation (personalization, comparison, and despair)
target_behavior.function: Avoiding comparison and judgment to lower shame and Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced social support, Increased sense of isolation, Negative self-evaluation maintained

target_behavior.behavior: Self-deprecation negative Automatic thoughts (such as 'I am too stupid' 'I cannot pass')
antecedent: Receiving news of or thinking about failing the bar exam
When planning or preparing to retake an exam
When comparing oneself with parents and peers in evaluation
target_behavior.core_reason: The core belief of 'I am not smart enough / incompetent' with overgeneralization, future prediction, and other cognitive biases
target_behavior.function: Avoiding strong disappointment and shame from failing again by lowering expectations (short-term Self-protection)
target_behavior.consequence: Learning motivation and Decreased efficiency, Career development hindered, worsened depression and Anxiety
